title: Singapore Airlines’ A380 suites offer privacy with trade-offs
text:
Singapore Airlines’ A380 suites offer privacy with trade-offs The daily brief for frequent flyers
 Today Topics Archive Up Front Singapore Airlines’ A380 suites offer privacy with trade-offs
 Singapore Airlines’ A380 Suites cabin gives six passengers a private setting with high walls, sliding doors and rotating seats. A review of a twelve-hour flight praised the design and crew but cited gate-security delays and the absence of showers. Book the Cook offers advance meal selection.
 Originally reported by turningleftforless.com · FLIGHT REVIEW: Singapore Airlines’ A380 Suites First Class – incredible, not perfect 
 Edited by Randy Petersen 
 Oct 25 · 11:00 PM · 1 min
 Key details Suite 4.64 square metres Fleet twelve A380 aircraft Seat 270 degrees of rotation Meal deadline at least 24 hours before the flight Each suite measures 4.64 square metres, and Singapore Airlines had twelve A380 aircraft in its fleet. The armchair rotates up to 270 degrees and reclines, while a tablet controls seating, lighting and entertainment. Carry-on storage and clothing space sit beside the entry; the aircraft has no overhead bins, helping preserve an open feel. Two-stage blinds filter sunlight or block it entirely.
 At Changi, first-class passengers can use Singapore Airlines’ Private Room, but security screening at gates in terminals other than Terminal 4 was described as slow, with no first-class priority during boarding. The review also says Book the Cook lets passengers choose from an expanded menu, provided selections are made at least 24 hours before departure; the service is also offered in business class.
 Why it matters The private suite provides space and privacy, but travelers should not expect shower facilities onboard. At Changi, lack of priority at gate security can make the departure process slower, while meal customization requires planning a day ahead.

 Related stories Singapore Airlines A380 business class offers comfort and quality 
 A recent flight review highlights Singapore Airlines’ A380 business class as unexpectedly comfortable despite online criticism. The cabin features spacious seating, a soft mattress pad even on short flights, and excellent catering via Book the Cook. Drink service rivals top carriers, with signature cocktails like the Singapore Sling served well.

 Aug 6
 Singapore Airlines trials concierge for first class 
 Singapore Airlines is testing a personal concierge service for first class passengers at Changi Airport. The trial begins at The Private Room lounge, offering gate transfers and security line assistance. No permanent rollout yet, but a decision is expected soon.
 via onemileatatime.com
 Aug 2
 A380 first class bathrooms rank highest 
 Six airlines offer standout first class lavatories, led by Emirates’ shower suites. These premium bathrooms feature amenities like heated floors, bidets, and urinals. Most are located on A380s, leveraging upper-deck space unused by seats.
 via onemileatatime.com
 Aug 23
 Singapore Airlines 787-10 loaded at Seoul airport 
 A Singapore Airlines Boeing 787-10, registration 9V-SCS, was photographed being loaded at Incheon Terminal 1 ahead of its return to Changi. The aircraft, delivered in April 2023, serves routes including Seoul, Tokyo, and Mumbai. It is one of 28 such jets in the carrier’s widebody fleet.
